newsitem.title: USA: General Motors plans to party into Hispanic market.
newsitem.headline: General Motors plans to party into Hispanic market.

text.p: General Motors Corp. will sponsor a day of events at Miami's South Beach as part of the city's Carnaval, the biggest Latin festival in the United States, in an effort to boost its sales to the Hispanic community there.
The event, on March 2, is a showcase for GM where it has lagged behind as the spending power of south Florida's Hispanic community has grown.
Hispanics make up at least 55 percent of greater Miami's population and a significant part of south Florida's.
"That translates into the majority of people who are looking to buy an automobile," Knox Ramsey, GM executive director for regional markets said.

The South Beach event will feature a parade, soccer matches, and Latin bands and dancing -- including an attempt to break the world record for the number of people dancing the Macarena. GM also plans to sign up more Hispanic dealers in the area.

General Motors, the world's largest car maker, has been slow to wake up to the spending power of Hispanics. While GM has a 31 percent market share nationally its share in south Florida is just 17 percent. Among the Hispanic community in south Florida it has only a 16 percent market share, according to Accentmarketing, which is handling the push for GM.
John Maciarz, GM's regional communications manager for the southern region, conceded that GM has to do a better job.
"Carnaval is an opportunity to do things better and differently. We wanted to shake off our somewhat staid and conservative image," he said.
